title: Expected rejection (adversarial fixture shape)
description: SEC-6 requires adversarial fixtures (injection attempts, unknown fields, type confusion, depth bombs) to 'produce clean rejections' — a distinct outcome from the successful expected/<backend>.artifact.json shape. An adversarial fixture case has expected/rejection.json instead of any backend artifact: no backend ever sees a compilable IR, because validation rejects the request before compilation.

rejectedAt.description: Which validation stage catches this case, in the pinned order from docs/architecture/c4-components-core-ir.md: allowlist -> limits -> coercion -> static injection. 'requestParsing' covers malformed-wire-shape cases that never reach IR validation at all (e.g. a filterModel referencing a nonexistent operator).

reason.description: The specific SEC-3/SEC-6/SEM-5/GRP-4 condition this fixture exercises. 'duplicate-output-name' (added #1886) is two aggregations resolving to the same GRP-4 output name: legal-looking on every backend and silently lossy on all of them, so it is refused in the shared AggregationValidator rather than by any one compiler. 'field-not-filterable' (added #1872, extended #1907) is a colId that IS in the schema's allowlist but declared FieldConfig.Filterable:false, referenced in a filter condition (filterModel/customFilters), as a setValuesRequest.colId, or (#1907) consumed as a groupKeys drill-down key — distinct from 'unknown-field' because the colId exists, it is merely disallowed for this use.

note.description: Optional free-text clarifying what makes this case adversarial and why it must be rejected rather than silently accepted (SEC-6's 'clean rejection' requirement).
